hero.subtitle: (Şehir Plancısı ve CBS Geliştiricisi)
hero.description: I develop Web-GIS applications. I work on organizing spatial data, presenting it on maps, and automating repetitive processes.

about.p1: With a background in Urban Planning and expertise as a GIS Developer, I combine the power of spatial data with modern web technologies. My goal is to transform complex geographical and urban data into clear, manageable, and interactive digital systems.
about.p2: I specialize in enterprise-level solutions, particularly in large-scale real estate portfolio management, urban regeneration feasibilities, and automation processes. I believe maps are not just visuals, but powerful decision support tools.

projects.p1_desc: An enterprise Web-GIS platform that manages real estate portfolios, spatially analyzes property data, and digitalizes processes. Parcels, real estate, zoning status, planning decisions, and project inventories are made analyzable via dynamic layers. A scalable architecture managed by role-based authorization consolidates multi-company and public data into a single database hierarchy. The platform's UI includes modules for spatial analysis, geometric properties, zoning compliance, project development, financial indicators, and external system integration. Interactive dashboards and thematic analysis tools were developed over a map, time, and attribute-based decision support system. Digital transformation of complex data from Excel, PDF, and physical documents was successfully executed.
projects.p2_title: ArcGIS Experience Builder Custom Widget Architecture
projects.p2_desc: Custom widgets were designed and developed to optimize enterprise GIS workflows on ArcGIS Experience Builder. User experience was improved by a Hierarchical Layer Manager allowing browser-side freezing of temporary data layers. A Dynamic PDF Reporting module enables instant corporate-template reporting of map views and analysis charts. Analysis tools were built to generate dynamic parcel query links from coordinate data via TKGM integration. Various widget components were produced featuring layer management, group filtering, smart search engines, data export, and admin panels.
projects.p2_detail_title: Advanced Layer Manager and Dynamic Reporting Module
projects.p2_summary: Developed with React and TypeScript for ArcGIS Experience Builder, this module manages map layers in a hierarchy, provides layer search and filtering, and exports selected spatial data to PDF and Excel formats.
projects.p2_feature1_title: Dynamic configuration and automatic data reading
projects.p2_feature1_desc: Layer and field selections are not fixed in the component code. Administrators select the required layers and fields in the Settings panel. The widget reads this configuration, builds its content from the map data, and can be used in different projects without code changes.
projects.p2_feature2_desc: Spatial query results are converted to PDF on the client side. Page layout, automatic pagination, and table styles are applied while the report is generated.
projects.p2_feature3_desc: Data received from map services is processed before the Excel file is created.
projects.p2_feature3_item1: Database field names are replaced with user-facing Alias labels.
projects.p2_feature3_item2: Unix Timestamp values are converted to DD.MM.YYYY format.
projects.p2_feature3_item3: Column widths are adjusted automatically according to cell content length.
projects.p2_feature4_desc: Layers and sublayers from map services are displayed in a tree structure. Users can manage layer visibility through this structure.
projects.p2_feature5_desc: Users can search and filter layers. Visibility and opacity changes are applied to the map view immediately.
projects.p2_feature6_desc: The interface uses jimu-ui and jimu-core components, allowing the widget to work with the Experience Builder theme and configuration system.
projects.p2_widget2_title: Topographic Slope and Synchronized Coordinate Tracking Tool
projects.p2_widget2_desc: The coordinate-slope widget calculates slope percentage and angle from the horizontal distance and the start and end elevations of a line selected on the map.
projects.p2_widget2_summary: The tool calculates the horizontal distance and elevation difference of a line drawn on the map. It uses these values to produce slope percentage and angle, while displaying coordinates during pointer movement.
projects.p2_widget2_image_alt: Interface of the topographic slope and coordinate tracking tool
projects.p2_widget2_feature1_title: Dynamic projection and horizontal distance calculation
projects.p2_widget2_feature1_desc: The start and end points of the line are read. Depending on the map's spatial reference, geometryEngine.geodesicLength or a planar calculation determines the horizontal distance between them.
projects.p2_widget2_feature2_desc: ElevationLayer.queryElevation() retrieves the start and end elevations above sea level.
projects.p2_widget2_feature3_desc: The absolute difference between the start and end elevations is calculated. Its ratio to horizontal distance is used to produce the slope percentage and angle.
projects.p2_widget2_feature4_desc: Frequent X and Y coordinate updates during pointer movement are limited with throttle and debounce methods, reducing unnecessary React state updates.
projects.p2_widget3_title: Corporate Identity, Secure Login-Logout and Session Management Module
projects.p2_widget3_desc: The user-profile-logout widget manages login, user profile, secure logout, and authorized page routing for ArcGIS Experience Builder applications in a single component.
projects.p2_widget3_summary: The module checks ArcGIS Enterprise credentials on the login page. After a successful session, it routes the user to the authorized map dashboard. In profile mode it displays user and role information, and clears existing security tokens during logout.
projects.p2_widget3_feature1_desc: The widget operates in Login Mode or Profile Mode according to the page configuration. The login screen and user profile are managed by the same component.
projects.p2_widget3_feature2_desc: OAuthInfo and IdentityManager check the ArcGIS Enterprise session. When authentication completes, Jimu Page Routing opens the authorized map dashboard.
projects.p2_widget3_feature3_desc: Logout clears the ArcGIS OAuth security tokens stored in the browser and routes the user back to the login page.
projects.p2_widget3_feature4_desc: The window.jimuConfig.isInBuilder check prevents automatic login or logout routing while a page is being edited. Routing runs only in the end-user environment.
projects.p3_desc: Data integration and management processes were executed via Python and ArcPy automation scripts, strictly preserving spatial data integrity. Digital transformation operations were carried out by converting complex data from Excel, PDFs, and physical documents without altering original content or headers. Pandas was utilized for large dataset processing, integration into the geodatabase structure, and automation of repetitive data preparation pipelines.
projects.p4_title: Open Source Web-GIS & Custom Mapping Applications
projects.p4_desc: I develop Web-GIS and interactive web applications. BirdMap brings bird observations and ecological traits together on a map. My real estate solutions project combines corporate presentations, mapped portfolios, and 3D project showcases in one application.
projects.p4_birdmap_desc: I developed BirdMap to explore bird records in Türkiye, ecological traits, and observation locations alongside their sources. The application combines bird search and filtering, map-based area analysis, shared-province planning, and species PDF exports in one workflow. The same React interface uses static files in the live release and an API with PostgreSQL/PostGIS in the local setup.
projects.p4_detail_title: BirdMap — Türkiye Bird Inventory and Spatial Observation Platform
projects.p4_environment: Live: static Vercel release · Local: Fastify + PostgreSQL 17 / PostGIS
projects.p4_summary: The 13 October 2026 reports describe 543 catalog entries: 505 counted species, 31 escaped/released entries, and 7 hybrids. Of these, 541 have locations and 536 have BIRDBASE trait mappings. This total does not represent 543 distinct naturally occurring bird species or an official, complete national checklist.
projects.p4_feature1_title: Dated observations and controlled data preparation
projects.p4_feature1_desc: The eBird Basic Dataset archive is filtered by Türkiye, approved records, scientific name, date, and valid coordinates. The main period is 1 August 2023–31 July 2026. Selected historical observations supplement 67 entries without locations in that period. The combined package contains 371,102 species-location summaries derived from 2,010,783 observation records; these are not counts of individual birds. Historical locations are not presented as evidence of current distribution.
projects.p4_feature2_title: Trait filters, information cards, and PDFs
projects.p4_feature2_desc: Birds can be filtered by name, classification, and ecological traits. BIRDBASE traits, nesting information, legacy catalog fields, and mapping information are organized through a 142-field dictionary. The information card shows a photograph, sources, and a diet radar chart. Species PDFs combine traits, the chart, overall distribution, and the map view at download time. Alternative taxonomy mappings and missing values are identified separately.
projects.p4_feature3_desc: Species within a province, radius, or drawn polygon are examined using grid-cell centers, so results near boundaries may be approximate. Shared-province planning instead uses provinces with observation locations for every selected species. Bird, province, and facility selections build a plan preview. The live release stores plans in browser localStorage; the local API version writes them to the database. Representative route–turbine analysis is not a scientific migration-risk assessment.
projects.p4_feature4_desc: A lightweight catalog loads first; species details and filter columns load as needed. Static location files are downloaded per species, then filtered to the visible area and sampled to a point budget in a Web Worker. Clustering and district files loaded on zoom limit rendering work. Zustand manages selections, layers, and panels; TanStack Query manages the data cache. Lists, information cards, maps, and legends share the same species identifiers.
projects.p4_feature5_title: One interface, two data access paths
projects.p4_feature5_desc: The interface uses React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet, and Geoman with a shared data access layer. The live Vercel release runs on JSON/GeoJSON files and Turf.js; it does not fetch real-time observations from the eBird API. Local mode connects to PostgreSQL/PostGIS through Fastify. A build setting selects the mode while preserving species identifiers. Map rendering of administrative boundaries still uses static file fragments in API mode.
projects.p4_feature6_desc: PostgreSQL 17 and PostGIS store species, traits, sources, observations, geometries, plans, and import records across 15 application tables. The eBird species code is the shared identifier; detailed observations and location summaries are stored separately. Parameterized SQL, connection pooling, GiST spatial indexes, and bbox/limit rules constrain queries. This infrastructure is used in the local API version.
projects.p4_feature7_desc: Observation locations come from eBird, ecological traits from BIRDBASE, facility and turbine layers from OpenStreetMap, and photographs from Wikimedia Commons. Geometries for 81 provinces and 973 districts are generated from the GDB package. Locations for two sensitive entries are protected; representative route and park geometries are off by default and shown as demo layers.
projects.p4_feature8_desc: The preparation pipeline preserves source versions, species identifiers, and file hashes; a new package is activated after validation. The 13 October reports record static/API parity checks for 543 detail records and 142 filter fields, database integrity checks, and browser workflow tests.
projects.p4_birdbase_desc: Compiled by Çağan H. Şekercioğlu and colleagues, BIRDBASE brings together ecological and life-history traits of birds worldwide. The v2025.1 release recorded in BirdMap's reports supplies information such as diet, habitat preferences, nesting, body traits, movement behavior, and conservation status. It is not the source of observation points or current distribution in Türkiye.
projects.p4_birdbase_item1: Scientific names and taxonomy mappings connect the data to eBird species codes. There are 509 direct and 27 alternative mappings; alternatives retain a review status. No species traits are inferred for the seven hybrids.
projects.p4_birdbase_item2: Traits support filters, information cards, diet radar charts, and species PDFs. BirdMap's 142-field dictionary is not simply a list of BIRDBASE traits: it also includes nesting details, legacy catalog fields, and mapping fields. Missing values, zero, and T for trace amounts remain distinct; global IUCN status is not treated as a Türkiye-specific risk score.
projects.p4_birdbase_item3: The dataset is licensed under CC BY 4.0 and the paper under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Author, version, and DOI references are retained with the source information.
projects.p4_birdbase_citation: Şekercioğlu, Ç. H. et al. (2025). BIRDBASE: A Global Dataset of Avian Biogeography, Conservation, Ecology and Life History Traits. Scientific Data. Paper DOI: 10.1038/s41597-025-05615-3; dataset DOI: 10.6084/m9.figshare.27051040.
projects.p4_ebird_desc: The Cornell Lab of Ornithology's eBird platform collects records submitted by bird observers. BirdMap's observations and locations are prepared from the July 2026 eBird Basic Dataset archive (EBD_relJul-2026). Species codes, observation dates, coordinates, and locality information come from this source, separate from the BIRDBASE layer used for ecological traits.
projects.p4_ebird_item1: The main data period is 1 August 2023–31 July 2026. Approved records from Türkiye are filtered using exact scientific-name matches and valid coordinates. Selected older observations for 67 catalog entries without locations are retained as a separate historical supplement, not as a continuous time series or evidence of current distribution.
projects.p4_ebird_item2: Detailed observations are stored in the local database, while species-coordinate summaries support the map. Location counts and observation-record counts are not counts of individual birds. Locations for two sensitive entries are withheld; observer identifiers, ORCID, and free-text comments are not imported.
projects.p4_ebird_item3: The live release uses dated static data prepared from the EBD archive. Recent observations in local API mode are a separate data feed supplied through the eBird API.
projects.p4_ebird_citation: eBird Basic Dataset, EBD_relJul-2026 (July 2026). Cornell Lab of Ornithology, Ithaca, New York. The Türkiye subset and selected historical supplement used in BirdMap are documented in the 13 October 2026 project/data reports.
projects.p4_ebird_dataset: eBird data products and EBD access information
projects.p4_luma_environment: React / TypeScript · 2D maps and 3D presentations · Static Vercel demo
projects.p4_luma_desc: I developed a web application covering different presentation needs for real estate firms and project developers. Corporate presentations, residential/commercial/land portfolios, single-project showcases, and a multi-project world share one entry point. The Luma Avlu and Vera Konakları examples connect maps, 3D buildings, unit selection, and information sheets. The demos use representative projects, prices, and locations.
projects.p4_luma_summary: Three solution families are demonstrated through four demos: corporate presentation, mapped portfolios, and 3D presentations for single or multiple projects. The initial catalog includes 9 projects and 4 individual properties; the Luma and Vera models contain 60 selectable units in total. Visitors can filter properties, move from map to model, compare units, and prepare a PDF information sheet for their selection.
projects.p4_luma_feature1_desc: Company information and residential, commercial, and land listings share one portfolio. Visitors browse category filters, galleries, features, additional descriptions, and property-specific media links. A request summary can be prepared for the selected property and shown to the visitor.
projects.p4_luma_feature2_desc: MapLibre displays projects and individual properties as points and land records as area geometries. Lists, maps, and property files share a synchronized selection. Filters cover sale/rental, price, rooms, land use, and recorded area. Land files include a north-oriented sketch and area information; searching the visible map region is a visitor action.
projects.p4_luma_feature3_desc: Luma Avlu's presentation leads from project imagery, location, courtyard, and architecture to unit exploration. Three.js and GLB models support block, floor, room, and sales-status filters. Selected units are highlighted in the list and model, with camera focus on the selection. Luma's 48 units and Vera's 12 units use a shared viewer.
projects.p4_luma_feature4_desc: Projects can be explored in geographic context with CesiumJS. Visitors navigate filtered projects, focus on a location, and approach the Luma/Vera models. Unit exploration opens in a separate Three.js view; returning preserves the selected project and applicable camera context. The world uses representative placements and a flat reference surface.
projects.p4_luma_feature5_title: Favorites, comparison, and PDF information sheets
projects.p4_luma_feature5_desc: Units can be saved as favorites and up to three options compared by area, floor, aspect, type, status, and price. Available plan diagrams appear in the unit file. PDF information sheets combine the selected model view, location map, and unit details with project-specific plan and document fields. Preferences are retained during navigation.
projects.p4_luma_feature6_title: Separate corporate and map content editors
projects.p4_luma_feature6_desc: The corporate and 2D map demos have separate content editors. Properties can be added, edited, hidden, and supplied with galleries and links. The map editor supports point placement, area drawing, and geometry editing. Demo changes are stored in the current browser; content can be exported as JSON and map records also as GeoJSON.
projects.p4_luma_feature7_title: Shared data model and connected navigation
projects.p4_luma_feature7_desc: Companies, projects, properties, blocks, floors, units, media, and model placements connect through shared identifiers. The 2D map, Cesium world, building model, and PDF use the same record. URL-based selection carries the correct project and unit between experiences. Model and plan content for Luma and Vera remains linked to its own project identifiers.
projects.p4_luma_feature8_desc: MapLibre, Three.js, Cesium, and PDF modules load when their experience opens. Hidden scenes pause, static 3D views render when something changes, and resources are released on close. Mobile layouts provide separate list, map, and file views. Guided camera exploration, a lightweight list view, and retry options for loading failures are included.
